# GPU learned frontier-ranker prototype (parallel to untimed SMT)

User approved building the prototype in parallel. Do not stop/restart the untimed solver PID1059154. Production5691617/default1041, simulator/tests and prior reports remain unchanged. No commit/push/cloud/submission or package installation. Use an existing ROCm PyTorch environment only after real GPU forward/backward smoke verification.

Question: can a small learned frontier policy produce a legal kernel below981 cycles, and does a transformer outperform a linear ranker and MLP?

Boundary: cloned lane-ready compiler; existing issue/capacity/engine rules stay authoritative. A callback may move one of the first four ready candidates to the first eligible position, preserving every operation and all other positions. Observe up to32 ready candidates, with structural features, readiness, baseline priority gaps, critical/load distances and pressure information. No raw instruction-ID embeddings, runtime tree contents or output values. No-op callback must reproduce981 exactly. Allocation<=1536 before lowering/execution is mandatory.

Data: six source graphs (original, final-XOR rewrite, and four declared one-cache-removal variants). Four training graphs, two held-out graphs. Record32 evenly spaced post-startup states per training graph and16 per held-out graph. Counterfactual teacher labels come from complete frozen-verified schedules with exactly one local action override; at most three alternatives per state, <=486 baseline/counterfactual evaluations total. Infeasible allocations get no cycle label and are never lowered/executed. Stop on feasible correctness or model-integrity failures.

Models: linear, two-layer MLP, two-layer width128/four-head transformer without positional embeddings. Train each for600 updates on the GPU with masked regression to measured cycle deltas; final fixed checkpoint, no held-out fitting. Batch64; holdout used only for reporting. This is a rollout-supervised policy prototype, not a claim of reinforcement learning or global optimality.

Screen: <=36 closed-loop evaluations (three models x original/rewrite x checkpoint-only/all-post-startup application x confidence thresholds0/0.5/1.5 cycles), followed by <=6 held-out evaluations with per-model settings selected on training graphs. Use CPU inference for tiny sequential rollout calls to avoid transfer overhead; GPU performs batched training/evaluation. Compare training fit, action changes, invalid allocation rate and actual frozen cycles. Preserve simpler/no-op controls. No additional search/training stages without a new decision.

Execution: max3 CPU rollout workers alongside the existing one-core SMT job; GPU PyTorch device0 must be confirmed RX7900XT. Torch CPU threads1; GPU allocation cap4GiB if supported. Finite configurations/update counts, no wall-clock cutoffs. Run persistent phases with progress files so interactive tool/session limits cannot cancel them.

Any new sub981 candidate, including a teacher counterfactual, requires100 full-width seeds, five patterns, independent lane/physical checks, repeated deterministic reconstruction, mutations, frozen/supplementary and source-only gates before calling it strongly verified. No production integration or saved-stream promotion. If only the teacher or a simpler baseline improves, report that honestly. If no winner, retain981.

gpu_smoke.device_identification: gfx1100 and20GiB match rocminfo RX7900XT; initial name-string assertion corrected after metadata-only failure

checks.full_promotion_gates: not run: representative984 is slower than retained981

run.remaining: Strong candidate gates if sub981; independent receipt review and decision report.
